what_it_does: Verilog is the low-level language chip engineers use to describe digital hardware circuits. AI language models can generate Verilog automatically, but they struggle because Verilog was underrepresented in their training data and because standard text-splitting (tokenization) chops Verilog code at word boundaries that do not match the language's logical structure. This paper applies 'speculative decoding' — a technique where a fast helper model drafts tokens and a larger model checks them in parallel, speeding up generation — but adapts the token-splitting to respect Verilog's syntax boundaries instead of arbitrary subword cuts. The result is claimed to be both faster generation and higher-quality Verilog output, because the model sees the code in chunks that match how the language actually works. Exact speed and quality numbers are not confirmed from the abstract.
